te-8756.question: Virata p. 9: tentative translation 'which man should I name as the lord of this circle of prabandha verse' and the reading of కధినాథునిగా as 'as lord of this work' (base అధినాథుడు): does it fit?

te-8757.question: Nirvachanottara p. 18: the transcription prints "బ్రచురముగ", probably for "ప్రచురముగ" (abundantly); should the card keep the printed spelling or the corrected one?

te-8759.question: The printed page prints a space inside this word as బెడం గై; the card writes బెడంగై, glossed 'beautifully' from the base బెడగు (beauty): please check the spelling and the gloss.

te-8762.question: The printed page has a space inside ధర్మోత్తరమును as ధర్మో త్తరమును; the card writes it without a space: is that right?

te-8764.question: The printed page has a space inside సైన్యోద్దాముల as సైన్యో ద్దాముల; the card writes it without a space. The base for ఏమగలును is మగడు and for బ్రతియె is ప్రతి: please check both bases and glosses.

te-8765.question: గుమతి is read as కుమతి ('evil-minded') and యనక as 'without saying' (base అను): these two glosses are the builder's tentative reading: please check them.

te-8766.question: The printed page has a space inside మదీయాగ్రపురోహితుఁ as మదీయాగ్రపురో హితుఁ; the card writes it without a space: is that right?

te-8767.question: The printed page has a space inside య ట్లగుటఁ as య ట్లగుటఁ with a space; the card writes యట్లగుటఁ. The word నేరిమిమెయి is printed unbroken and is glossed 'by skill': please check the gloss.

te-8800.question: తిద్దరాని (tiddarāni) is glossed "that cannot be measured or grasped" in the old layer; it now reads "that cannot be set right, beyond reproach": please check the gloss.
ముద్దుగారే (muddugārē) is glossed "darling, from a verb meaning to overflow with charm; said to the child" (the verb is ముద్దుగారు (muddugāru)): please check the gloss and its source form.

te-8805.question: The last line's gloss 'call them in, won't you' (పిలువరే) is tentative, and the base for పెక్కుచేఁతలు is చేత (cēta): are both right?

te-8806.question: The couplet's archaic grammar (కట్టునా, 'would bind'; గాలిఁ బోవుఁ, 'will be blown away') is tentative, and the assertive గాక is glossed 'will surely, indeed' (tentative): is the English right?

te-8807.question: The assertive particle గాక is glossed 'will surely, indeed' (tentative), as in te-8806, and the verbs బెనఁగేను and పొరలేను are read as first-person future: is the rendering right?

te-8808.question: The base lemma నేరు for నేరనయితిఁగా and the gloss 'could not, was not able to' are tentative: are both right?

te-8812.question: గగనాధిప is glossed 'lord of the sky' (tentative): is the gloss right?

te-8813.question: The word వశిష్టుడు is joined from two printed lines (వ / శిష్టుడు); the edition field says so: is the join right?

te-8816.question: గుణమేలరా is glossed 'this behaviour' (tentative): is the gloss right?

te-8852.question: లాడుచు (lāḍucu) is glossed as part of కలకలలాడు (kalakalalāḍu), to look bright and lively: is that the right sense in this line?

te-8853.question: The Hemalatha sentence is in bookish spelling: are the modern forms listed in the layer note right?

te-8854.question: The exclamation యేమిపాటరా (yēmipāṭarā) is given the base పాట (pāṭa) (song), meaning what a song: is that the right base and sense for an exclamation?

te-8855.question: The sentence has no tentative base; the note says the stabber counts thirty-three stabs. Is the actor-role reading in the note right?

te-8857.question: The line mixes English words in Telugu script, such as మైడియర్ (maiḍiyar) and షేక్స్పియర్ (ṣēkspiyar), and the page does not show who speaks it. The base వేలవేయు (vēlavēyu) for వేలవేసినావ్ (vēlavēsināv) (sulking) is tentative: is the sense right, and is the speaker known?

te-8858.question: On page 26 Janghala Sastri is the speaker of this line, as the sentence before it shows. The line is printed యిదిగో (yidigō), not the modern ఇదిగో (idigō), and the word వార్తాపత్రిక-నాకుఁ (vārtāpatrika-nāku) keeps its hyphen as printed. Is the printed form right on the card?

te-8859.question: The idiom పప్పు (pappu) వుడకదు (vuḍakadu) is glossed as a plan that will not succeed: is that the sense Girisam means here?

te-8860.question: The base పాసు (pāsu) (pass, as in an exam) and the sense severely for చావ (cāva) (base చావు (cāvu)) are tentative: are those senses right?

te-8861.question: The first printing year 1916 is from the Telugu Wikisource author page's list of works; the card's edition is the 1934 second edition. Is 1916 right as the work's date?

te-8862.question: The page is Page quality level 1: raw OCR, not proofread. Its spelling, including the joined word లోకములో (lōkamulō) (లోకంలో (lōkaṁlō) today), must be checked against the scan; a proofread page should replace this card if one is found.

te-8864.question: The date 1946 is the first of the two years the Telugu Wikisource author page lists for the novel (1946, 1978); 1978 is the edition. Is 1946 right as the work's first printing?

te-8865.question: The word వింటూంటే (viṇṭūṇṭē) is given the tentative base వినుట (vinuṭa) (to listen), with the sense keep listening, obey: is the sense right?

te-8866.question: The verse word లానఁగఁ (lānaga) is given the tentative base ఆను (ānu) (to become): is the base and sense right? The page marks the verse with ఆ. (ā.), read as the ātaveladi metre: is that reading of the marker right?

te-8867.question: The essays' dates 1913 to 1933 come from the Telugu Wikisource author page, which says they were published in Suvarnamukhi and Andhra Patrika. Is this the work's date the reviewer would show?

te-8900.question: Vemana's dates are not settled: English Wikipedia gives c. 1652 for his birth and no death year, Wikidata gives 1652 to 1730, and Telugu Wikipedia gives c. 1367 to 1478 with question marks. te-8901.question: ద్విజుడు (dvijuḍu) is glossed "twice-born; will become twice-born" with the note that the verse uses it for a worthy person, not for birth: please check the sense and the note.

te-8903.question: కొంచఁబోడు (koñcabōḍu) is now read as కొంచు (koñcu) "taking along" plus పోడు (pōḍu) "will not go", with the base కొంచుపోవు (koñcupōvu) glossed "to take along" and the English "he will not take even a cowry shell along with him": the reviewer is about 80% sure of this reading, please check the base and the English line.

te-8904.question: జల్లగాను (jallagānu) is glossed "calmly, softly" and the verse is rendered as a contrast with bronze: please check the English rendering of the second line.

te-8906.question: The second line gloss 'ఓగుబుద్ధి' (ōgubuddhi) is read as 'a foolish mind' by the builder, and the verb sense of ఈలేదంచు is 'saying he did not give': please check both readings against the printed page.

te-8909.question: The word నొనర (nonara) is glossed 'well, truly' by the builder, a guess from context: please check the gloss. The word ఉపమ (upama, in నుపమగలదు) is glossed 'a likeness': please check whether it means a simile or a means.

te-8910.question: The first word అన్నిగోసివేసి (annigōsivēsi) is glossed 'having cast off all' by the builder, the word గోసి being unclear: please check the sense of the first line.

te-8912.question: In దానములను జేయఁ దన చేతులాడక (the last line), మొదలు is glossed 'the capital, the principal' by the builder: please check the sense of the closing line.

te-8913.question: The phrase పసిరికాయపురుగు (pasirikāyapurugu) is read as 'a worm in an unripe fruit', and the ruin of the learner is compared to it: please check this sense.

te-8914.question: The phrase రాజయోగంబులు (rājayōgambulu) is rendered 'royal yogas' in the native rendering and the base gloss, not in the note, which the builder read as the virtues of a king: please check the sense.

te-8915.question: The verb నణఁగియుండు (naṇagiyuṇḍu) is glossed 'is humbled, subdued' by the builder, from context: please check the sense of the first lines.

te-8917.question: The compound చూపుచూచు (cūpucūcu) is a compound of 'show' and 'see'; the builder glossed it 'shows, and looks on': please check the gloss.

te-8950.question: The Telugu of te-8950 to te-8969 is copied from te.wikisource's transcription of Carr's 1868 supplement (the scan was not reachable): please check the spelling of each proverb against the printed page.

te-8959.question: బాపడు (bāpaḍu) is the printed word for a Brahman: is the gloss "Brahman" and the informal register right for a learner card?

te-8968.question: The printed proverb has బందువూ (banduvū), an old spelling of బంధువు (bandhuvu, relative): should the card keep the printed spelling or the modern one?

te-9003.question: The printed proverb joins అన్నీ (annī) and తెలిశినవాడూ (teliśinavāḍū) into one run (అన్నీతెలిశినవాడూ, annīteliśinavāḍū); the card writes them as two words: please check the spacing against the printed page.

te-9008.question: కాని (kāni) in this proverb is read as "bad, unfavourable" (కాని కాలం, kāni kālaṁ, a bad time): is that the right sense for a learner card?
కాని (kāni) in this proverb is read as "bad, unfavourable", as in కాని కాలం (kāni kālaṁ), a bad time: is that the right sense for a learner card?

te-9019.question: The printed proverb has అడిగా (aḍigā), which the card keeps; the gloss "must you ask?" is the builder's own reading: please check the spelling and the meaning.

te-9051.question: The printed proverb has అబద్దము (abaddamu), spelled with a plain d where card te-3603 has అబద్ధం (abaddhaṁ): the reading and IPA follow the tool for the printed spelling, so they differ from the card: please check the spelling against the printed page.

te-9054.question: The printed proverb has ఆయుధము (āyudhamu), an old spelling of ఆయుధం (āyudhaṁ), and తెడ్డే (teḍḍē) is glossed "paddle; ladle": please check the spelling against the printed page and the gloss.

te-9055.question: The meaning "eats like an ox and sleeps like a log" for ఎద్దువలె (edduvale) and మొద్దువలె (modduvale) is the builder's reading (an idler, not a worker): please check the sense and the gloss of మొద్దు (moddu).

te-9058.question: The proverb opens with తల్లి (talli) and బంగారు (baṅgāru): the literal "even if the mother were gold" and the gloss "does not stop stealing" are the builder's own reading: please check the sense of the first clause.

te-9062.question: జంగం (jaṅgaṁ) is glossed "jangam (ascetic)" with a note that a jangam is a Lingayat ascetic: please check the gloss and the note.

te-9063.question: తవిటి (taviṭi) is glossed "coarse (flour)" and రొట్టి (roṭṭi) "flatbread": is that the right sense for a learner card, and is the comparison of a mother's plain cooking with a wife's feast rendered fairly?

te-9064.question: The meaning "outward decoration does not change what a thing is" for పిల్లకు (pillaku) and గోడకు (gōḍaku) is the builder's own reading: please check the sense.

te-9066.question: బెబ్బే (bebbē), a dismissive interjection, is glossed "nothing" in the English: please check the gloss and the English rendering.

te-9068.question: The printed run కాస్తారుచూతాము (kāstārucūtāmu) joins two words in one spelling and is read as one word: please check the spacing and the gloss "will tend (we will see)".

te-9069.question: The printed proverb has కష్టము (kaṣṭamu), an old spelling of కష్టం (kaṣṭaṁ), and యేండ్లు (yēṇḍlu), printed with an older spelling of ఏండ్లు (ēṇḍlu): please check both spellings against the printed page.

te-9270.question: ఋ (ru) is taught as said ru (the course's reading). Is that how it is said today, or r̥ or rɯ in some speech?

te-9275.question: ఙ (ṅa) and its example వాఙ్మయం (vāṅmayaṁ, literature): how common is ఙ as a letter, and is a better example word in use? The note says only that it is rare.

te-9276.question: చ (ca): Wikipedia, after the JIPA illustration, says native words with చ before a back vowel are said ts. The card teaches tʃ only. Which words, if any, should say ts?

te-9279.question: ఝరి (jhari, stream; waterfall) is the example for ఝ (jha): is it a word a learner would meet, and is the gloss right?

te-9299.question: వ (va): the card says a soft sound between English v and w (ʋ). Is that the right description for a beginner?

te-9301.question: శ (śa) is said sh on the card and often s in colloquial speech. Wikipedia says శ is said s in Standard Telugu and most dialects: which should the card teach first? Same question for ష (te-9302) and స (te-9303).

te-9304.question: హ (ha): the card says the h of 'head'; Wikipedia's IPA help page writes a voiced ɦ. Which is right between vowels?

te-9307.question: The six double-consonant cards (te-9307 to te-9312) say a double consonant is held longer: is there a better plain description, and are the example words the clearest?

unit_level.question: ఱ (ṟa) and the other te-sounds contrast pairs with no card yet (the double consonants beyond the six, 14 pairs in all) are deferred: the course has no modern word or tool support for ఱ. Should a later pass add them?

zh-4322.question: Tone of the first 一 in 一心一意 (yī xīn yí yì): written yī, though 一 before a fourth tone is yí in most words. Is the chengyu pattern right?

zh-4352.question: Tone of 一 in 一丝不苟 (yī sī bù gǒu): written yī, not yí. Is that right?

zh-4365.question: Tone of 一 in 别具一格 (bié jù yī gé): written yī before a second tone. Is that right?

zh-4369.question: Tone of 一 in 背水一战 (bèi shuǐ yī zhàn): written yī before a fourth tone. Is that right?

zh-4592.question: The note gives the rank order 助教, 讲师, 副教授, 教授. Is that the right order in mainland academic titles?

zh-4593.question: The note says a 助教 helps with marking (批改). Is that the usual role in a university?

zh-4601.question: Part of speech of 学术 is noun; it also comes before a noun as an adjective (学术会议). Is noun right?

zh-4606.question: Part of speech of 答辩 is verb and the note gives a second sense (a formal reply to a charge). Should the second sense stay in the note?

zh-4607.question: Is 导师 used for a thesis supervisor in the sense the note gives?

zh-4611.question: Is 考研 (a short form of 考研究生) natural as a dictionary entry, or should it be listed under 考试?

zh-4651.question: The note says 八宝饭 is served at festivals. Is that right for the New Year table?

zh-4670.question: The note says in Cantonese tea houses 点心 is dim sum. Is that accurate for a learner's first meaning?

zh-4672.question: The example says bitter food is thought good for the body. Is that a fair statement, or should it be cut?

zh-4673.question: The note says 味道 is felt by the tongue while 香味 is smelt. Is that the right distinction?

zh-4677.question: The note says a whole fish is served at New Year because 鱼 sounds like 余 (surplus). Is that cultural claim right and worth keeping?

zh-4681.question: Traditional form 滷 was typed by hand: please check it.

zh-4682.question: The note calls 腊肉 a speciality of some southern regions. Which regions are most known for it?

zh-4686.question: The second example says southern people eat sweet dumplings at the winter solstice. Is that a fair generalisation?

zh-4687.question: The note says many foods are eaten at particular solar terms. Is that a fair statement for the cards' examples?

zh-4693.question: The note calls 米线 a speciality of the south-west. Is that the right region?

zh-4696.question: The note says 饮茶 means to have a tea meal with dim sum in Cantonese. Is that the usual sense in speech?

zh-4698.question: In the example 边 is used for 'while' (我喜欢边喝茶边吃茶点). Is that natural?

zh-4722.question: The second example says 我们在课上学了怎么押韵. Is 课上 natural here, or should 上课 be used?

zh-4751.question: The second example says readers wait each week for the next instalment of a serial. Is 等下一期连载 natural?

zh-4755.question: The note says 隐喻 is the metaphor that says one thing is another, and 比喻 the general word. Is that split right, and is 他是一头牛 (he is a hard worker) a fair example?

zh-4786.question: The second example says 饭好了，大家快出来吃饭. Is 出来 with 吃饭 natural for calling people to a meal?

zh-4819.question: The first example, 我们等到明天再说, is glossed as 'let us wait until tomorrow to talk about it'. Is that the natural sense of 等到?

zh-4823.question: The second example says 他最近变好了很多. Is 变好了很多 natural, or should a different word be used?

Are the eleven spoken and written pairs right in meaning and register (举行/开会, 禁止/不能, 取消/不开会了, 通知/告诉, 支付/付钱, 参加/去开会, 感谢您/谢谢你, 光临, 已/已经, 及/和, 均/都)?

已, 及 and 均 have no cards of their own, so they are bases glossed as written-style words. Is 老师及学生均参加会议 a natural written sentence?
Is the ladder 你 + verb (blunt), 请 + verb (polite), 麻烦您 + verb + 一下 (a favour) right, and is the warning that 请 to a close friend sounds distant fair?
Do the six pairs (不是...吗, 难道, 怎么, 谁, 哪里, 什么) keep the meaning of the plain statement, and is the claim that they sound sharp to a stranger or elder fair?
The note says rhetorical questions are said with a firm falling voice. Is that right for 难道 and 怎么 questions? Also, is 您好，请进 natural for welcoming a guest?

source.date for each Analects, Mencius and Xunzi card is the creator's lifespan, not a date for the text: the works were compiled after their authors' lifetimes and no compilation date was read. Is a lifespan range acceptable as source.date for these works?

Compound words without their own Wiktionary entry (for example 春眠, 夜来, 花落, 不亦, 学而) have their pinyin composed from the readings of their characters, each read on en.wiktionary for its traditional form; tone changes (不, 一) follow the course rule, not a dictionary entry. A reviewer should check the composed readings.
一 as a base word (zh-6010 還 / 一岁一枯荣 in zh-6012) carries the tone-sandhi readings yí and yì; en.wiktionary lists yī, yí and yì only as citation forms. Check.
